title: The Future of Local News
text:
Local newspapers play an important role in keeping communities informed. Reporters spend many hours interviewing witnesses and checking official documents before they publish a story. In recent years, however, many small papers have been forced to close because advertising revenue has declined. As a result, some towns now have no regular source of independent news.

Some researchers argue that online news sites can partly fill this gap. Their reports often appear within minutes of an event, which makes them attractive to readers. However, the same speed can lead to errors that are corrected only later. For this reason, many editors insist that every article should be verified before it is published.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, why have many small newspapers closed?
options: Readers have stopped buying papers in cities
Official documents are no longer available

questions.text: What do reporters do before they publish a story, according to the first paragraph?
options: They interview witnesses and check official documents
They publish the story within minutes
They ask editors to verify the article

questions.text: What can be inferred about towns that have no local newspaper?
options: They may have fewer sources of independent news
They receive more accurate online reports
They have more advertising than before
They rely only on official documents

questions.text: What is the writer's likely attitude toward online news sites?
options: Certain they will replace printed papers

paragraph_translations: Los periódicos locales desempeñan un papel importante para mantener informadas a las comunidades. Los periodistas pasan muchas horas entrevistando a testigos y revisando documentos oficiales antes de publicar una noticia. Sin embargo, en los últimos años muchos periódicos pequeños se han visto obligados a cerrar porque los ingresos por publicidad han disminuido. Como resultado, algunas ciudades ya no tienen una fuente regular de noticias independientes.

Algunos investigadores sostienen que los sitios de noticias en internet pueden llenar en parte este vacío. Sus informes suelen aparecer en cuestión de minutos después de un suceso, lo que los hace atractivos para los lectores. Sin embargo, esa misma rapidez puede provocar errores que solo se corrigen más tarde. Por esta razón, muchos editores insisten en que cada artículo debe ser verificado antes de publicarse.
